purpose: Measure false alarms under a known unchanged score distribution, detection under controlled score shifts, and routing tradeoffs. No historical test data are inputs.
generation: Draw a new reference and independent batch per replication from the profile. Use separate seeded streams for reference scores, latent batch scores, replacement uniforms, and label uniforms. Replace scores with 0.05 according to each scenario probability. Correctness probability is 0.55 + 0.45 * score - accuracy_penalty. Benign shifts use the unchanged latent score for correctness. Pair all scenarios within a replication.
oracle: Known-population diagnostic uses the true generating histogram, with the same released calibration and floor. It is not an implementable estimated-reference correction.
analysis: Report stable alarm proportions and per-cell 95% Wilson Monte Carlo intervals, controlled-shift detection, pooled routing counts and accepted risk, additional reviews, and accepted errors withheld by the gate relative to the identical threshold-only rule. Intervals describe simulated trials, are not simultaneous, and do not establish deployment guarantees.
decision_rule: Do not optimize thresholds on these results or on historical FIN/FiNER-ORD tests. If finite-reference alarms substantially exceed the known-population diagnostic, prioritize reference-uncertainty-aware calibration in a separate prospective experiment. Do not change the default numeric floor based on this simulation alone. Label-only failures require labeled monitoring, not score-only threshold tuning.
